findings.title: [corrected on verification] New test's docstring promises timeline-event visibility the test never asserts
findings.evidence: Docstring: "The timeline itself still renders (the invite + takeover events stay visible); only the future-promise hint is dropped." Assertions present: refcheck-taken-over-landlord_ref, "You're handling this one", hint-absence — no timeline-entry assertion.
findings.detail: VERIFIED with corrected framing: both lenses claimed an over-correction gutting the whole attempt log would pass — FALSE: the export affordance (refcheck-export-landlord_ref) renders inside view_attempt_log and is asserted by the existing taken_over_row_shows_label_chips_and_export_test, so block removal fails the suite. Residual true claim: individual timeline entries (Invitation sent / taken-over label) are unasserted on a taken-over row while the docstring says they stay visible.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert a timeline entry on the taken-over row (e.g. string.contains("Invitation sent") |> should.be_true) or trim the docstring to what is asserted.

findings.title: Hint-absence assertion hardcodes the escaped literal instead of the copy constant
findings.evidence: html |> string.contains("Next reminder in ~2 days if there's no reply") |> should.be_false — vs client/src/copy.gleam:663: pub const refcheck_what_happens_next: String = "Next reminder in ~2 days if there's no reply"

findings.recommended_fix: Derive the escaped expectation from copy.refcheck_what_happens_next in both the new and existing assertions.

findings.title: Post-takeover staleness window: hint persists until the one-shot refetch lands (and indefinitely if it fails)
findings.evidence: #(m, effect.batch([refetch_refcheck_effect(model), toast_eff])) — refetch_refcheck_effect fires a single fetch_application_detail; no local taken_over_at update, no retry.
findings.detail: VERIFIED accurate mechanism. Pre-existing architecture (same one-shot refetch for every row action), not introduced by this diff. In the window the badge and hint still AGREE (both read model taken_over_at via the same taken_over() predicate), so the fix's core invariant holds; the only stale artifact is the hint beside a success toast. A local-model fix would breach the briefing's panel-only scope guard.
findings.recommended_fix: Out of scope for this PR; if desired later, apply the action response payload (or a taken_over_at local update) in the success handler for all row actions.
